newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi treating jailed British nurses justly - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Saudi treating jailed British nurses justly - envoy.

text.p: Britain's ambassador to Saudi Arabia expressed confidence on Tuesday that two British nurses charged with murder in the kingdom were being treated justly, Saudi state television reported.

It quoted Andrew Green as saying at a press briefing at the Home Office in London that "the case of the two British nurses accused of committing an act of murder in the kingdom was being investigated minutely."
He said that the two nurses were "being treated fairly and justly."
Deborah Parry, 41, and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, have been charged with the murder of Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford, 55, at a hospital complex in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province in December.
They could face public beheading by the sword if convicted.
"The British Ambassador said that the Saudi line based on Islamic Shari'a treated all foreigners equally without discrimination," the television said.
The ambassador said the case was in the Saudi judicial process and "we are waiting for the court to issue its verdict", it added.
His comments came one day before Saudi Arabian Defence Minister Prince Sultan is due to arrive in London for talks that will cover a wide range of issues.
